bib.title: Swag: A Large-Scale Adversarial Dataset for Grounded Commonsense Inference
bib.venue: Proceedings of the 2018 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing (EMNLP), pages 93-104

read.skipped: none; the PDF has no appendix (it says details are in the appendix, which is not included)

question: Can a large multiple-choice dataset for grounded commonsense inference be built that is easy for humans but hard for models, despite annotation artifacts?
hypothesis: Adversarial Filtering against stylistic classifiers removes annotation artifacts, so models cannot solve the task by style alone while humans still can.
contributions: Task of grounded commonsense inference unifying NLI and commonsense reasoning
Adversarial Filtering (AF), iterative de-biasing against an ensemble of stylistic classifiers
Empirical comparison of many models and analysis showing headroom

method.summary: Pairs of consecutive video captions (ActivityNet Captions, LSMDC) give a context and a true ending; an LSTM LM oversamples 1023 negative endings per context, AF keeps the 9 hardest against stylistic models, and Mechanical Turk validates. Many NLI/sentence-encoder models are then trained and tested on it.
method.task: 4-way multiple-choice next-event prediction (choose the verb-phrase ending)

datasets.name: Swag
datasets.source: ActivityNet Captions (20k YouTube clips, 203 activity types) and LSMDC (128k movie captions); videos not used
datasets.preprocessing: Second sentence split into NP and VP with a constituency parser; drop sentences with rare tokens (<=3 occurrences), short (l<=5) or no verb phrase; examples with <=3 non-gibberish endings filtered

datasets.name: BookCorpus
datasets.source: pretraining of the LSTM LM generator

models.name: LSTM LM candidate generator
models.architecture: LSTM language model conditioned on context
models.init_from: pretrained on BookCorpus then finetuned on video captions

other.folds: five LMs trained, one per set of training folds, so none sees its own found endings

models.name: AF stylistic ensemble
models.architecture: MLP on LM perplexity and lengths + bag-of-words + 1-layer CNN (filters 2-5) + BiLSTM over top-100 words with POS tags for rare words; concatenated and passed through MLP

models.name: ESIM+ELMo
models.architecture: ESIM with 1024d ELMo, output layer size 1 with softmax over endings

models.name: Other baselines
models.architecture: fastText, SkipThoughts, InferSent, 2-layer BiLSTM, DualBoW, Decomposable Attention, SNLI-ESIM, Length, ConceptNet rule system

training.objective: multi-class cross-entropy for learned models (binary cross-entropy for fastText); AF ensemble trained jointly with cross-entropy

other.AF: N_easy=2, N-=1023 negatives refined to k=9, 80%/20% train/test split per iteration; Fig 2 runs ~140 iterations, first 100 with the MLP only (read from Fig 2)
other.training_sets: found endings only, or found plus highly-ranked human-validated generated endings
other.details: the paper defers hyperparameters to an appendix not included in the PDF

inference.decoding: LM sampling is greedy sampling of 1023 unique endings, not beam search (beam biases toward low perplexity)
inference.samples: 1023 negative endings per context; human eval: 5 Turkers x 100 questions, majority vote

metrics.name: accuracy
metrics.definition: fraction of questions where the model picks the gold ending out of 4

eval.protocol: Val and test accuracy; input ablations: ending only, second sentence only, context+second sentence; human: 5 MTurk workers on 100 questions plus an expert (first author); no seeds or significance tests stated

prompts.text: Imagine that you are watching a video clip. The clip has a caption, but it is missing the final phrase. Please choose the best 2 caption endings, and classify each as: likely, unlikely, gibberish

results.claim: Best model ESIM+ELMo trained on found+gen with context reaches 59.2% test accuracy
results.setup: Swag test, context+2nd sentence, found only training, ESIM+ELMo
100 sampled questions, 5 MTurk workers, majority vote

results.claim: fastText gets only 29.0% on Swag versus 67.0% on SNLI, showing few lexical biases
results.setup: fastText, Swag test, ending/second sentence input
results.note: Text quotes SNLI fastText 67.0% vs 34.3% baseline (Gururangan et al 2018)

results.claim: SNLI-pretrained ESIM bottlenecked through entailment gets 36.1% on Swag
results.setup: SNLI-ESIM with log-linear on 3-way probs, test

results.claim: Adversarial Filtering drives stylistic-ensemble accuracy from about 60% to near random chance
Error analysis: turkers preferred gold over ESIM+ELMo's wrong choice 94% of the time; most common reason situational
results.setup: 100 random val questions ESIM+ELMo got wrong, 5 Turkers each
results.quote: they preferred the gold endings 94% of the time
results.note: Table 4 prints Situational 53.7% while text says 52.3%; weirdness 18.1% in table vs 17.5% in text

results.claim: Turkers rank the found ending best or second best 73.7% of the time
results.setup: MTurk validation, one found plus five adversarial endings

results.claim: Generated endings marked gibberish by humans 9.1% of the time
results.quote: marked as “gibberish” by humans only 9.1% of the time

limits: Adversarial models are purely stylistic and look at the second sentence only; authors concede subtle artifacts likely remain (5.4)
Hyperparameters and LM architecture are deferred to an appendix not in the PDF
Human performance measured on only 100 questions; most labels have one annotator
Filtering only on style; semantic implausibility not filtered (footnote 4)
Later work (not in this PDF) showed pretrained LMs largely solve Swag; not stated here

terms.definition: iterative refinement of a set of negative assignments to increase the entropy under a chosen model family, replacing negatives the model gets right with ones it gets wrong

lineage.work: Annotation artifacts in natural language inference data
Hypothesis Only Baselines in NLI (Poliak et al.)

code.snippet: A_i^easy = {j in A_i : f_theta(x_i^+) > f_theta(x_{i,j}^-)}; replace N_easy easy indices with adversarial k not in A_i satisfying f_theta(x_{i,k}^-) > f_theta(x_{i,j}^-)
